video_title: Why I'm Not Buying Duolingo Stock (Yet)

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: So, given the threat from artificial intelligence, Duolingo's management team has chosen its response. What is it? Well, they're focusing on attracting customers even at the expense of monetization.
claims.reasoning_summary: In response to the AI threat, management is prioritising customer acquisition (more freemium features) over monetization; management said it may have over-emphasised monetization and profitability before.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: So, what this means for investors is likely increasing customer engagement, increasing daily active users, which management has targeted 100 million over the next couple of years.
claims.reasoning_summary: The strategy likely raises customer engagement and daily active users, but at a cost to monetization whose size is a big question mark.

claims.speaker: host
claims.horizon_original: over the next couple of years
claims.evidence_text: increasing daily active users, which management has targeted 100 million over the next couple of years.
claims.reasoning_summary: Management targets 100 million daily active users over the next couple of years.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: Duolingo was doing great in expanding its business, growing from around 100 million in revenue in 2020 up to over 1.15 billion over the trailing 12-month period.
claims.reasoning_summary: Revenue grew from about 100 million USD in 2020 to over 1.15 billion USD over the trailing 12 months.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: And they have been improving profitability meaningfully since 2022 when its operating margins were negative 30% and then soared to 14.2%.
claims.reasoning_summary: Operating margin improved from -30% in 2022 to a record 14.2% after post-2022 cost discipline.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: Before the threat of artificial intelligence and the increasing effectiveness and increasing competition from not just AI, but you know, other language conversion offerings from various tech companies has reduced the need to learn a language completely.
claims.reasoning_summary: AI and translation offerings from tech companies reduce the need to learn a language, threatening the business.

claims.speaker: host
claims.certainty_original: likely ... or perhaps even start declining
claims.evidence_text: That being said, this new strategy of focusing on customer acquisition at the expense of profitability and monetization is likely to cause Duolingo's margins to at least remain where they're at, or perhaps even start declining back downwards.
claims.reasoning_summary: The customer-acquisition strategy will likely keep margins at least flat at the 14% record, perhaps declining.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: We've already seen some of that decline happening in its returns on invested capital, which were approaching 40% and have fallen to 30%. And these are significant improvements from 2021 when it was at -30%. So, it's likely to continue downward
claims.reasoning_summary: ROIC has fallen from near 40% to 30% and is likely to keep falling in the near term, though still more than twice the cost of capital.

claims.speaker: host
claims.condition: if they indeed attract as many customers as they think they will attract with this new policy
claims.evidence_text: But that downward trend is likely only in the near term if they indeed attract as many customers as they think they will attract with this new policy. Longer term, the return on invested capital could trend higher and return to levels before at the peak, even above their previous peak.
claims.reasoning_summary: If the strategy attracts as many customers as hoped, ROIC could trend back to or above its previous peak longer term.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: the share price has recovered significantly since the lows reached in April when the share price fell to around $89. It's now recovered back to $143
claims.reasoning_summary: The share price recovered from about 89 USD at the April low to 143 USD.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: It's trading at a forward PE of 19. This is still near the lowest level the stock has traded for going back a few years. So, despite the share price improvement, the increase in earnings per share and expectations for earnings per share is making Duolingo stock look slightly undervalued even considering the elevated risks.
claims.reasoning_summary: At a forward P/E of 19, near the lowest in a few years, and with rising EPS expectations, the stock looks slightly undervalued despite elevated risks.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: And that caused the fair value to increase to $149. The current market price is 143. So it looks fairly valued.
claims.reasoning_summary: Updated DCF (lower risk estimate) gives a fair value of 149 USD vs 143 USD: fairly valued, not undervalued after his 5-10% (or larger) margin of safety.

claims.speaker: host
claims.evidence_text: And so given the company's elevated risks at a fair value, I would wait for a better entry price to buy Duolingo stock. So I will be reiterating this hold rating on this business today.
claims.reasoning_summary: Given elevated risks at a fair valuation he would wait for a better entry price to buy and reiterates his hold rating.

warnings: Duolingo has no ticker mapping in the curated tables and no ticker was spoken or shown in the title, so the claims stay unresolved.
